chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had intercourse with his wife while he was fasting and she was fasting, he said: 'If he compelled her, then upon him is two expiations; and if she consented to him, then upon him is one expiation and upon her is one expiation; and if he compelled her, then upon him is the striking of fifty lashes, half the hadd; and if she consented to him, then he is struck with twenty-five lashes and she is struck with twenty-five lashes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the expiations and punishments for a fasting couple who have intercourse during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific legal consequences for a married couple engaging in intercourse during Ramadan, distinguishing between compulsion and consent to determine the distribution of expiation (kaffarah) and corporal punishment (jald). It highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance where the husband bears a heavier burden of expiation if he compelled his wife, whereas both share equal liability if she consented, reflecting the principle of individual accountability within the marital unit.
